entries.name: ✝ (inaccessible name)
entries.notes: DECIDED (editor): §E.2 books `✝` at unit 03 (04-funext) as a "first sighting", but §D.0 mandates that x02 is scaffolded with `intro ⟨h3, _⟩`, and the goal Lean really prints after it carries a `right✝`. Split like `⟨…⟩`: it APPEARS at 00-aliasing, deliberately unexplained — that is the exhibit, not a violation — and is EXPLAINED at 04-funext, then named properly at 22-exec. 00-aliasing owes the reader one clause saying the name is not theirs to type.

entries.name: runIf
entries.notes: NOT a migration — no `def runIf` exists in content/, lean/ or the fragments. Edition 1 quotes a goal state from a declaration that is not in the repo, so that goal state is unverifiable. The author of 24-interpreter either (a) writes the variant interpreter — the `ite` case spelled with `if` instead of `match`, about fifteen lines — compiles it, and RE-DERIVES the goal, in which case the re-derived goal wins over Edition 1's quoted one if they differ; or (b) drops the comparison and says so in their summary. It is an optional lab unit, so it is their call. What they may not do is quote a goal state nobody can reproduce.
